This is the one-day course on the EU-frames case with the tools of data science in the foreground: R, the IDE, data management, a Quarto report and version control. The case is the material for all of them. It is a study of Eurobarometer surveys, which asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the member states frame the European Union, with a claim of the original author (OA) that five analysts reanalysed in the Multi100 project. After a short opening on why reproducible tools matter, the morning takes the toolchain apart and gives you a first session in R on the country-year panel of the case. In the afternoon you check how that panel was built from sixteen survey files, and the R work reaches its target. You reproduce, to the third decimal, the result that Multi100 recorded for one of the three analysts whose analyses rest on means of countries or of cells, whichever you choose, read the code that the analyst deposited, and put the reproduction into a report that somebody else can rerun.

You leave able to find your way around an IDE, to read, filter, summarise and draw a data frame in R, and to write the checks that a panel built from many files needs, with a reproduced result in a rendered report or in your notes. The day ends with one look at the curve of alternative analyses of the claim, as the reason that readable code matters, but it has no menu of specifications and sends nothing to a class chart, because the [one-day course on methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does both.

## How you work

The day is taught mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. It works on aggregate data only, the country-year panel of the course and two files that the course rebuilt for two of the analysts, and the lab holds all three. Open it in a tab of its own and keep this page open beside it. Each part of the day has a page that lists its steps in order, and every step that you work at the keyboard has a button that opens the lab at the right task, or the page on which the work is done. This is the format in which the downloadable workspace, opened in an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), gives you most, because the IDE and the report are the subject of half the day. If you have not installed it, you follow those stretches on the shared screen and do the R in the lab. The slides are on the [slides page](slides.qmd), and each part opens with a link to its place in the deck.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The class sends some of its answers in the chat at the same moment, so the day needs a facilitator.

## The parts of the day

- **[Before the day](before.qmd)** (about an hour, more with the installation). You read the case study and open the browser lab once, and you install R, an IDE and the workspace if you can, since this day uses them most.
- **[Part 1 – Credibility and software](part-1.qmd)** (ninety minutes). The part sets out the three Rs and the five analysts of the claim, whose disagreement could be diagnosed because their code runs, then takes the toolchain layer by layer and ends with R running on your machine.
- **[Part 2 – R and the IDE](part-2.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). The R tutorial is worked live, the IDE follows in six steps, and the part ends with a first session of your own on the panel.
- **[Part 3 – Data management and the reproduction](part-3.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after an hour for lunch). The part goes from sixteen survey files to one panel and the checks that catch slips, and then you reproduce the result of C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL and read the code that your analyst deposited.
- **[Part 4 – The report, version control and archiving](part-4.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). You put the reproduction into a rendered report, watch how a project keeps its versions, take one look at the curve of the claim, and find where finished work is deposited.
- **[After the day](after.qmd)** (as long as you like). The page says where to go next.

[Start with Before the day](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The same case is also taught as one-day courses on [open science](../eu-frames-one-day-open-science/index.qmd) and on [methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd), as a [three-day course](../eu-frames-three-days/index.qmd) that builds the data from the raw survey files, and as a [self-study route](../self-study/index.qmd).
